name: Barbell Reverse Curl
summary: A standing elbow-flexion exercise using an overhand grip to target the brachialis, brachioradialis, and forearm extensors.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Grip the barbell with an overhand (pronated) grip at approximately shoulder width.
Allow the bar to rest against the front of your thighs with your arms fully extended and elbows tucked close to your torso.
steps: Brace your core and lock your upper arms firmly against your sides.
Curl the bar upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your wrists neutral and firm throughout the ascent.
Continue lifting until your forearms are nearly vertical and you achieve a strong contraction in the brachialis and forearms.
Lower the bar under control along the same path back to full elbow extension.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you curl the bar up; inhale as you lower it under control.
cues: Keep knuckles facing forward and wrists rigid.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Control the descent; don't let the weight drop.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso to use momentum.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load, brace your midsection, and keep your torso upright throughout the set.

common_faults.fault: Letting the wrists bend backward into hyperextension under load.
common_faults.correction: Actively squeeze the bar and keep the wrists straight or slightly extended to protect the joint.

common_faults.fault: Drifting the elbows forward or flaring them wide.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper arms locked in place beside your ribcage to isolate elbow flexion.

precautions: If straight-bar pronation causes outer wrist or forearm discomfort, switch to an EZ-bar to reduce joint strain.
